task_read: A very long-horizon build of a complete Excel-style spreadsheet product spanning many largely independent subsystems: persistent HTTP server, a REST contract that must be reverse-engineered from an existing client (/dev_tests/helpers.py), a 100+ function Excel-365 formula engine with dynamic-array spill/LET/LAMBDA/iterative calc/goal-seek, dirty topological recompute under hard performance budgets, XLSX/CSV round-trip graded against LibreOffice ground truth, a Playwright-targeted SPA, and WebSocket collaboration. Difficulty comes from enormous breadth, an under-specified wire contract, a non-exhaustive smoke suite versus a large hidden grading suite, and semantic fidelity to Excel. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily and continuously in all five meta-work faculties — this task sits near the ceiling of complexity.

dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reconnaissance
dimensions.description: Reverse-engineering the exact wire shapes from /dev_tests/helpers.py and probing Excel/openpyxl/LibreOffice semantics before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The JSON contract (ids, cell kinds, spill fields, patch/fill/sort/filter bodies, listing envelope) is defined ONLY by the existing client; guessing it wrong makes every endpoint fail the hidden suite regardless of internal correctness. Excel edge-case semantics and openpyxl/LibreOffice XLSX behaviour are graded cell-by-cell, so they must be studied, not assumed.

anchors.0: Starts coding endpoints/engine without reading helpers.py or run.sh; invents wire shapes and function semantics from memory.
anchors.3: Skims helpers.py once, picks up a couple of obvious shapes, but leaves most request/response bodies, cell discriminators, and spill fields inferred by guess.
anchors.5: Reads helpers.py and run.sh to pin down the main endpoints and cell shapes before building the core, and checks Excel semantics for the common functions.
anchors.8: Systematically extracts the full contract from the client (every endpoint, the kind discriminator, spill/spill_range, error names, locale params), cross-references it against the spec, and deliberately investigates hard corners (spill ghosts, LWW seq ordering, openpyxl definedName/numFmt/cellXfs requirements) before committing to a design.
anchors.10: Builds a durable, referenceable model of the entire contract and its ambiguities from the client plus targeted experiments (e.g. probing openpyxl/LibreOffice round-trip behaviour, Excel error-propagation and locale rules), continuously returning to re-read the client when a new subsystem is reached rather than acting on stale assumptions — reconnaissance that visibly prevents whole classes of contract-mismatch failures.

dimensions.name: Subsystem decomposition & sequencing
dimensions.description: Breaking the enormous surface into an ordered hierarchy of subsystems with dependency-aware sequencing and explicit done-criteria per milestone.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The product has a dozen loosely-coupled subsystems with real dependency order (server+persistence → cell model → recompute → formula engine → dynamic arrays → advanced surfaces). Attacking it as one undifferentiated push, or in the wrong order, guarantees thrash and a server that never reaches a runnable, gradable baseline.

anchors.0: No decomposition; jumps between unrelated features (a distribution function, then a WebSocket, then styling) with no ordering or completion criteria.
anchors.3: A flat undifferentiated list of features with no dependency ordering and no per-item definition of done.
anchors.5: A sensible component breakdown that front-loads a runnable server (health, persistence, core cells) before advanced features, with rough ordering.
anchors.8: An explicit dependency-ordered milestone structure where each milestone is independently checkable (e.g. 'health+persistence green', 'core patch/recompute passes run.sh', 'spill engine', 'xlsx round-trip'), and later subsystems are deliberately staged behind their prerequisites.
anchors.10: A living, hierarchical plan that sequences by both dependency and grading leverage, keeps a always-runnable server as an invariant between milestones, and is re-cut as understanding grows — each milestone carrying a concrete acceptance check that ties back to the client/hidden-suite surface.

dimensions.name: Verification beyond the smoke suite
dimensions.description: Deliberately designing checks — running run.sh, exercising helpers.py, restart/persistence tests, openpyxl re-import, Excel-value spot-checks — well beyond the non-exhaustive suite provided.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec explicitly warns the dev_tests are a non-exhaustive smoke suite and grading is a much larger hidden suite plus a LibreOffice ground-truth corpus. Passing run.sh proves almost nothing; only self-built verification against Excel semantics, round-trip fidelity, restart survival, and performance budgets catches the failures that actually cost points.

anchors.0: Never runs the server against the client or run.sh; assumes code is correct because it was written.
anchors.3: Runs run.sh occasionally and treats a green smoke suite as done; no independent checks of semantics, round-trip, persistence, or performance.
anchors.5: Runs run.sh/helpers.py regularly and does ad hoc manual checks of a few endpoints and formula results as features land.
anchors.8: Builds targeted checks the suite omits — Excel-value comparisons for formulas/errors, openpyxl re-import of exports, a process-restart persistence test, and at least rough checks against the performance budgets — and uses them to gate milestones.
anchors.10: Establishes a sustained verification harness spanning the graded dimensions (cell-by-cell value checks vs known Excel results, XLSX round-trip through openpyxl, collaboration seq/replay invariants, iterative-calc convergence, large-workbook timing), runs it continuously, and treats a discovered gap as a signal to strengthen the checks — verification that demonstrably surfaces defects a smoke run would miss.

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across the surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate done-vs-remaining picture across a dozen subsystems and 100+ functions, and detecting stuck/circular states.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With a surface this large over a long horizon, it is easy to lose the plot — forget an entire subsystem (locale, pivots, data validation), silently regress an earlier one, or sink hours re-debugging one function while dozens remain. Accurate progress tracking is what keeps effort flowing to the highest-value remaining work.

anchors.0: No sense of what is done vs outstanding; features are forgotten or rediscovered by accident.
anchors.3: Vague recollection of progress; no explicit tracking, so whole areas silently go unaddressed.
anchors.5: Keeps a checklist of subsystems/functions and updates it as things are completed, catching most omissions.
anchors.8: Maintains an accurate, regularly-updated map of completed vs remaining work across all subsystems, notices when a subsystem is stalling or when a change regresses an earlier one, and reallocates rather than grinding.
anchors.10: Sustains a precise, continuously-reconciled picture of the whole surface over the long horizon — detecting circular re-debugging early, confirming earlier subsystems still pass as new ones land, and using the remaining-work map to drive sequencing decisions to the very end.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on divergence
dimensions.description: Revising design, library choices, or approach when evidence contradicts assumptions — wrong contract shape, failing round-trip, blown performance budget, broken recompute.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Big up-front bets here (formula-eval library, OOXML library, recompute architecture) can prove wrong only once exercised — a library that won't round-trip openpyxl-readably, a recompute that misses the 100k/5000-dependent budgets, a contract detail read wrong. Barrelling ahead on a falsified assumption wastes the horizon; timely correction salvages it.

anchors.0: Ignores contradicting evidence; keeps building on a broken approach even as failures accumulate.
anchors.3: Reacts only to hard crashes with local patches, never revisiting the underlying design or library choice that caused them.
anchors.5: When a check fails, diagnoses and fixes the immediate cause, and will swap an approach when clearly forced to.
anchors.8: Treats failing checks (wrong wire shape, failed round-trip, missed timing) as signals to revise the design or tooling choice deliberately, and does so before piling more work on the shaky foundation.
anchors.10: Anticipates which bets are risky, validates them early with cheap probes, and when reality diverges performs a clean, scoped pivot (architecture or library) while protecting already-working subsystems — repeatedly converting falsified assumptions into corrected direction rather than sunk-cost thrash.

dimensions.name: Effort allocation for graded coverage
dimensions.description: Allocating limited effort across a surface too large to perfect, so that broad graded coverage is secured before any one area is gold-plated.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task is deliberately larger than can be finished flawlessly and is graded on a broad hidden suite, so the payoff structure rewards breadth-first partial credit (many subsystems working plausibly) over depth-first perfection of a few — a genuine allocation decision distinct from mere ordering.

anchors.0: Sinks the whole budget into one subsystem (e.g. exhaustively perfecting statistics/distributions) leaving most of the product unbuilt.
anchors.3: Follows the spec top-to-bottom with no regard for value density, over-investing in low-leverage corners while high-value subsystems go missing.
anchors.5: Roughly balances effort, getting most major subsystems to a working state before polishing.
anchors.8: Deliberately triages by graded leverage — secures a broad working baseline across all subsystems first, then deepens the highest-value or riskiest areas, consciously time-boxing rabbit holes.
anchors.10: Runs a disciplined value-density allocation throughout: continuously weighing remaining effort against expected graded coverage, deferring or stubbing low-return corners, and reallocating as new information about difficulty and payoff arrives — maximising total coverage under the horizon rather than local perfection.
